intent: token_audit reports what share of API messages carried more than one tool call, so batching discipline is measured by a tested code path instead of an ad-hoc script.
scope: Non-goal: changing how turns or cost are counted; reconciled totals are untouched
changes: Turn gains message_id and tool_calls; the docstring records that the harness writes one JSONL record per tool_use block, all sharing message.id
attribute.Batching dataclass counts messages/batched/calls grouped by message_id and exposes share and per_message
report.py renders a Tool-call batching section and persists tool_messages, batched_messages and batched_calls in the snapshot so the next run has a baseline
Axes was at the 12-attribute pylint cap, so the counters were grouped rather than suppressed; the test helper was split into _tool_turn rather than raising the arg-count limit

verification.evidence: 122 passed (was 116; 6 new tests cover both Batching branches and the zero-message guard)
All hooks pass; ruff/pylint findings were fixed by refactor, no suppressions added
Tool-call batching: 439 of 23,650 messages carried >1 call (1.9%), 1.02 calls/message. Reproduces an independent hand count over the same window.

risks: message_id is empty on records that predate it; those turns are skipped, so the denominator counts only messages that can be grouped
The autopsy's 7% lifetime batching figure is computed per record, not per message_id, so the two are not directly comparable
rollback: git revert the commit; the axis is additive and nothing else reads the new fields
Re-run python3 -m python_pkg.token_audit and confirm WEEKLY.md renders without the batching section
